rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e1: This is a study by Nikolai Grigoriev, from 1930. White to play and win.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e2: White starts by advancing the b-pawn just one square. If the king waited now, the black pawn would go to b4 and trade the pawns; the c-pawn keeps its move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e3: The black king goes to a5, next to its pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e4: Now the white pawns no longer have a quiet move, with no capture and no loss, to pass the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.1: The king comes too close: soon the black king will have no squares.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.2: The black pawn advances to b4. Notice: the white king on a7 takes a6 and b6 from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.3: The c-pawn advances. The black king on a5 has nowhere to go and is not in check: stalemate, a draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.1: On b7, the king is also too close and will leave the black king without squares.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.2: The black pawn advances to b4. From b7, the white king controls a6 and b6, the black king's escape squares.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.3: With the c-pawn advance, the black king is trapped on a5, not in check. It is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.b3b4.1: The b-pawn advances with check and spends the move it should keep.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.b3b4.2: The black king retreats to a6. If the c-pawn advances, the black pawn captures it: the reserve tempo is gone.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.c3c4.1: The c-pawn goes to a square where the black pawn can capture it.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.c3c4.2: The black pawn captures on c4. After White recaptures, one white pawn is left with the black king close to it: a draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! The king passes the turn without taking any square from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to bring the king to b8: it passes the turn without taking squares from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not one we are studying here. Let's go back to the position.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.volta: Let's go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l1: A move like this is called a waiting move: it changes nothing important and just hands back the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l2: Now Black plays, and no Black move saves the position: the white king waited without taking squares from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l3: The black pawn advances to b4 and tries to trade the pawns before the white king comes closer.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l4: Now the c-pawn does advance. No black pawn can stop it, and the black king cannot go to b5.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king goes back to b6, near the c4 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l6: The white king goes around the black king on the right, heading for the b4 pawn; the black king follows, always facing it.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l7: In the corner, the white king goes down the h-file, heading for the b4 pawn. The black king cannot follow to the edge: it must watch the c4 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l8: Along the third rank, the white king comes back and reaches d3, next to the c4 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l9: The white king goes to d4 and protects the pawn's advance to c5. With the king on c4, the b4 pawn will fall, and White wins.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l10: Let's go back to the question position. Why b8, and not a7 or b7?
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l11: On a7 or b7, the white king would take a6 and b6 from the black king. After the pawns advance, it would be stalemate.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l12: Remember: when the pawns can no longer pass the turn, the king makes the waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.curiosidades: Nikolai Grigoriev (1895–1938), from Moscow, was a player and composer of endgame studies, above all pawn endings. This study is from 1930: the win depends on a king waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's look at another example. Here no pawn can move: they are all blocked.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e2: White wants to capture the pawns on d5 and d6. The black king on c7 protects d6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e3: With no reserve tempo, the king takes care of the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f7.1: On f7, the king leaves two squares between the kings, an even number, and Black can leave the odd number.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f7.2: The black king goes to b7: three squares between the kings on the seventh rank, and Black has just moved.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h7.1: On h7, the king leaves four squares between the kings, an even number, and Black can leave the odd number.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h7.2: The black king goes to b7: five squares between the kings on the seventh rank, an odd number, and Black has just moved.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f6.1: The king goes to f6, and the black king can stay on the same rank, with an odd number of squares between them.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f6.2: The black king goes to b6, on the same rank. If the white king goes to e7 or g7, the black king returns to c7.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h6.1: The king goes to h6, off the seventh rank, and the black king can wait without giving way.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h6.2: The black king waits on b6. If the white king goes to g7, it answers on c7; if it goes to h7, on b7.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f5.1: The king goes down to f5 and moves away from the seventh rank, where the opposition is fought for.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6f5.2: The black king goes to b7. If the white king returns to e6, the black king goes to c6 and protects d5 and d6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6g5.1: The king goes down to g5 and moves away from the seventh rank, the way it needs to enter.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6g5.2: The black king goes to b7 and waits. If the white king returns to g6, the black king takes c6, next to both pawns.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h5.1: The king goes down to h5 and moves even further from the d-pawns.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.g6h5.2: The black king waits on b7 and copies every step: if the white king goes to h6, it goes to b6; if to g6, to c6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! The king goes to g7, on the black king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to g7, on the black king's rank: three squares between them, and Black to move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not one we are studying here. Let's go back to the position.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.volta: Let's go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l1: Notice: the white king went to g7. It seems to waste time, but it is a waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l2: Three empty squares between the kings on the seventh rank, an odd number: White has the distant opposition.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l3: The black king goes to b7 and tries to change the count of squares between the kings.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l4: The white king follows to f7: again, three squares between the kings.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l5: The black king returns to c7, next to the d6 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l6: Now the white king steps into e7: direct opposition, and the black king must give way.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l7: The black king goes to c6 and protects both pawns, d5 and d6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l8: The white king goes to e6 and attacks d5 and d6. Any black king move leaves one of them unprotected.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l9: The black king goes to b5, and the white king captures the d5 pawn. White wins.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l10: Let's go back to the starting position. Going to g7 passed the turn to the black king, like a reserve tempo, but with the king.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.1: First position: the same structure, but now the black king is on c6 and the white one on g7.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.2: There is more than one way to win. Let's look at the waiting move on the edge.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.3: The white king goes to f8, on the edge: a waiting move.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.4: The black king goes to b7 and tries to change the count of squares between the kings.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.5: The white king answers on f7: three empty squares between the kings on the seventh rank, and Black to move.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.6: The black king returns to c7, and the white king steps into e7: direct opposition.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.7: You already know the rest: on e6, the white king attacks d5 and d6, and one of them will fall.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.8: The d5 pawn falls. On the edge or away from it, the king waiting move handed over the turn at the right time.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.1: Now thinking from Black's side, and the board has turned. In the position of Grigoriev's study, imagine the white king went to a7.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.2: It came closer, but took two squares from the black king: a6 and b6.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.3: The black pawn advances to b4.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.4: If the c-pawn advances, the black king has no moves and is not in check.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.5: It is stalemate, and stalemate is a draw.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.6: And what if White captures on b4?
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.7: The black king captures back and, on the next move, also captures the b3 pawn. It is a draw.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.8: In defence, an attacking king that comes too close may stalemate the defending king. That is why, in the study, the white king waited on b8.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.fim: The b-pawn waited, the c-pawn kept its move, and your king found the right square without stalemating the black king.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.c3c4.1: The c-pawn advances too early and offers itself to capture.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.c3c4.2: The black pawn captures on c4, and your b-pawn cannot recapture. One pawn is left on each side: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b2b4.1: The b-pawn advances two squares and spends at once the waiting moves it was keeping.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b2b4.2: The black king goes to b6 and watches the b4 pawn. With no pawn move to pass the turn, your king cannot advance: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8a7.1: The king moves before the pawns have done their job.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8a7.2: The black pawn advances to b4 and trades the pawns. One white pawn is left with the black king close to it: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8a8.1: The king waits in the corner, but the b-pawn has not yet spent its move.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8a8.2: The black pawn advances to b4 and forces the trade: one white pawn is left with the black king nearby, and it is a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8c8.1: The king comes closer too early: Black still has the pawn move to answer with.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.b8c8.2: The black pawn advances to b4. Traded or not, the c-pawn does not win with the black king so close: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.c3b4.1: The c-pawn captures on b4 and breaks up the pawn pair that held the black king.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.c3b4.2: The black king goes to b5, captures the b4 pawn and then threatens the one on b3: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8c8.1: The king comes closer, but the black pawn can still capture on c3.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8c8.2: The black pawn captures on c3 and is free to promote. Your king is too far away: Black wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8a7.1: The king goes to a7 and lets the black pawn capture on c3.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8a7.2: The black pawn captures on c3 and runs to promote; your king cannot catch it: Black wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8a8.1: The king waits in the corner, but the capture on c3 is available.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.b8a8.2: The black pawn captures on c3, nobody catches it, and it promotes: Black wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.c4c5.1: The c-pawn advances one more square and comes within the black king's reach.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.c4c5.2: The black king captures on c5 and then goes for the b3 pawn: Black wins.
The king goes to b7 and takes from the black king the two squares it had, a6 and b6.
The black king has no move and is not in check: stalemate, a draw.
The c-pawn advances without the king's escort.
The black king goes to b5, reaches the c5 pawn and captures it: a draw.
The king goes to a7 and controls a6 and b6, the black king's last squares.
The black king has no moves and is not in check: stalemate, a draw.
The king goes to b7 and takes the squares a6 and b6 from the black king.
The black king has no move and is not in check: stalemate, a draw.
The c-pawn advances alone, far from the king.
The black king goes to b5; the pawn advances to c6, and the king captures it: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7g6.1: With that move, your king leaves four squares between the kings, an even number.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7g6.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7f7.1: With that move, your king leaves the white king's rank.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7f7.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h7.1: With that move, your king goes to the edge and loses time.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h7.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h6.1: With that move, your king goes to the edge, far from the road to the white pawns.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h6.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7f8.1: With that move, your king retreats and loses time.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7f8.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7g8.1: With that move, your king retreats and loses time.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7g8.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h8.1: With that move, your king retreats and loses time.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.g7h8.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.h5h4.1: With that move, your pawn spends early the push that should have been kept.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.h5h4.2: The white king heads towards its pawns and arrives in time to defend them: Black no longer wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king went to f6: three squares between the kings, on the same rank, and the turn passes to the white king. The h5–h4 push stays kept for later.
